name: openrouter-media-audio-embed
purpose: OPENROUTER's media transform, the half that actually rewrites the body: embedOpenRouterMedia (prompt-converters.js:1336-1370) turns an `audio_url` content part whose url starts with `data:` into `input_audio {format, data}` and DELETES the `audio_url` member, mapping audio/mpeg to mp3 and audio/wav to wav and defaulting any other mime type to mp3. The pinned caller passes `{audio: true, video: true}` for this source (chat-completions.js:2373). Both data-URL mime branches are in one scenario because their outputs differ only in the `format` member, and a build that hardcoded mp3 would differ on the second part.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.rule: value replaced with Bearer <redacted>, presence and scheme preserved
tier2.reason: The scenario supplies a synthetic key; the header's presence and scheme are the contract, the value is not.

tier2.rule: the recorder origin is replaced with <mock>
tier2.reason: OPENROUTER has no reverse_proxy and no custom_url: chat-completions.js:2302 is the hardcoded literal, so the pinned leg can only reach the recorder through the probe transport redirect and the Go leg through its seam. The PATH is untouched and IS compared.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
